chapman.notes: 5 species (M as third body, so 4 state species), 7 reactions (4 ARRHENIUS, one with M as reactant and product; 3 USER_DEFINED photolysis). Generator: median of 5 runs, specialized mode 0.025 s, generic-table mode 0.025 s (make bench runs both, with python3 3.13.1). Generated C: specialized 304 lines / 12126 bytes (build/ts1_model_specialized.c); generic tables 41 lines / 3395 bytes (build/ts1_model.c). make bench from make clean: median of 3 = 0.89 s (0.93, 0.89, 0.88); first run 1.05 s; TS1 for comparison 3.11 s. clang -O3 compile of the generated files alone: specialized 0.058 s, generic 0.046 s. Both programs: 540 internal steps (9 per 60 s interval), 0 rejected; one-thread elapsed for the 60 timed steps 0.341 ms generic, 0.21 ms specialized (single runs, not a benchmark).
chapman.generated_kernels_note: 4-cell run: generated kernels ran. Code path (src/solver.c): the tests that select the generated kernels involve neither the cell count nor the group size. chem_solver_create (lines 862-863) computes each cell's rate constants with kernels->rates whenever the model has a kernel table. evaluate_rhs (255-258) calls kernels->evaluate when there are no constraints and kernels->species_count == pattern.n and kernels->pattern_nonzeros == pattern.nnz. solve_group (673-682) installs kernels->factor and kernels->solve under the same size test when the factor and solve callbacks are the defaults, which chem_rosenbrock_default sets and benchmark.c never changes. Cell groups only split cells across threads and share one step size; every cell goes through the same per-cell calls (line 700), so this entry has no full-group or vector-width path to fall back from. ts1_bench_specialized links .kernels=&chem_generated_kernels (pattern_nonzeros 14 for chapman, 743 for both CB5 variants). Dynamic check: lldb and sample could not attach (developer mode is off; both waited for authorization and were killed), so a diagnostic driver (kernel_check/kernel_check.c, 132 lines, public kinetics.h API only) linked the same solver sources and generated model. It copies chem_model with the generated kernel table, keeping its sizes but wrapping each function with a counter, and runs the same problem (same CSV and cell count, group size 0, 1 thread, warm-up plus 60 steps of 60 s). 4 cells: rates 4, evaluate 4,392, factor 2,196, solve 6,588 generated-kernel calls. These equal the solver's totals (function_calls 1,098, decompositions 549, solves 1,647 including the warm-up) times 4, so every call was generated. The driver's final state is byte-identical to ts1_bench_specialized's.

difficulties: None in the entry itself: the benchmark programs (src/benchmark.c) are generic over the generated chem_model, and the generator (tools/generate_c.py) accepted all three converted files unchanged; no warnings in any build. The entry's mechanism JSON is close to the canonical one: the converter only nests rate parameters under 'parameters', turns [name, yield] product pairs into {name, yield} objects, moves the initial temperature, pressure, concentrations (species 'initial') and rate-parameter values ('custom_parameters') to where ts1.json keeps them, and writes molecular_weight 0.0 and diffusion_coefficient null (not in the canonical input; only SURFACE reactions read them). M stays in reactant and product lists with third_body true, as in TS1's O2 + M + O -> O3 + M. One deviation from the setup: 'make env' does not use an existing environment here; it creates a fresh conda env (python 3.12.11, pyyaml 6.0.2) from conda-forge with a package cache inside the worktree, which needs the network. Run with CONDA_OFFLINE=true it failed (PackagesNotFoundError: python=3.12.11), so it was not run online; the Makefile then falls back to python3 (3.13.1), which suffices because the generator needs PyYAML only for YAML configs. TS1_JSON is defined with := and is not documented as an override (the README documents 'make mechanism CONFIG=...', which builds only a generic library), but GNU make's command-line override works. Addendum (64 cells): lldb and sample both hung waiting for debugger authorization (developer mode is off) and were killed. The generated-kernel use was therefore shown with a 132-line diagnostic driver that wraps the public kernel table with counters; it plays no part in the reported comparisons, which come from the benchmark programs.
